claims.text: 5th Avenue & James Street had 147 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 1 person killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $10.1 million a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 4.4 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.5 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 3.0 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.0 million a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 5th Avenue, James Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
